Case_18002/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Growth of the organism on a MacConkey agar plate after 24 hours of incubation. Translucent colonies are seen.

description.short_caption: Growth of translucent colonies on MacConkey agar after 24 hours of incubation.
description.detailed_description: The image shows a MacConkey agar plate with visible growth of translucent colonies after 24 hours of incubation. The plate is held by a gloved hand, and the colonies appear as pale, non-lactose-fermenting growths against the pinkish background of the agar. The translucent nature of the colonies suggests the organism does not ferment lactose, which is consistent with the selective and differential properties of MacConkey agar.

Case_18002/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Growth of the organism on a blood agar plate after 24 hours of incubation. A translucent flat colony that spreads across the plate is seen.

description.short_caption: Growth of translucent, spreading colonies on blood agar after 24 hours of incubation.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a blood agar plate with growth of translucent, flat colonies that spread across the surface of the medium. The colonies appear to have a smooth texture and demonstrate a spreading pattern, consistent with an organism capable of motility or surface expansion. The plate is held in a gloved hand, and the background is neutral, emphasizing the culture plate.

Case_18002/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Growth of the organism on Hektoen enteric agar plate after 24 hours of incubation. Translucent colonies are seen.

description.short_caption: Growth of colonies on Hektoen enteric agar after 24 hours of incubation.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Hektoen enteric agar plate with visible bacterial growth after 24 hours of incubation. The colonies appear translucent and are distributed across the streaked sections of the plate. The green coloration of the agar is characteristic of Hektoen enteric medium, which is used to differentiate enteric pathogens. The plate is being held by a gloved hand, indicating proper laboratory handling.

description.short_caption: Triple sugar iron (TSI) agar slant showing differential fermentation results.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a TSI agar slant in a test tube after 24 hours of incubation. The slant has a red (alkaline) appearance in the aerobic portion (top) and a yellow (acidic) appearance in the anaerobic portion (butt), indicating glucose fermentation but no sucrose or lactose fermentation. The medium is tilted to display the color changes clearly. The test is used to differentiate bacterial species based on their carbohydrate fermentation and gas production.

yellow coloration in the butt (acidic reaction)
no visible gas production or black precipitate

description.short_caption: Lysine iron agar slant showing results after 24 hours of incubation.
description.detailed_description: The image shows a lysine iron agar (LIA) slant in a test tube. The slant portion is purple, indicating the absence of lysine deaminase activity. The butt of the slant is brownish-yellow, suggesting the absence of lysine decarboxylase activity. This pattern is consistent with organisms such as Shigella spp., which are negative for both lysine deaminase and lysine decarboxylase.
visible_findings: purple slant indicating no lysine deaminase activity
brownish-yellow butt indicating no lysine decarboxylase activity
clear separation between slant and butt
